name: Three Rings
shortDescription: A UK not-for-profit volunteer-management system for charities and community organisations, with rotas, a volunteer directory, team communications and controlled document sharing.
suitableContexts: Churches coordinating recurring volunteer shifts and teams
Churches that need a volunteer directory, rota and communications in one service
Churches seeking a general charity-sector system rather than church-specific member management

pricing.summary: Three Rings bases annual prices on an organisation's turnover. Its current account page says a typical small helpline or volunteer-run library would pay about £174 a year including VAT from April 2025, while a major national charity is likely to pay about £270 including VAT; the supplier says the smallest or new organisations may be eligible for free access. Confirm the applicable annual invoice, VAT treatment, SMS-credit cost and any dedicated-server charge before purchase.

gdprInformation: Three Rings CIC publishes terms identifying the church or other client as controller and itself as processor for system data. Its public statements describe UK-based application storage, UK and EEA backups, encrypted connections, access controls, action logging, a named DPO and an email sub-processor arrangement. The current terms say client data can be exported or destroyed at termination; request the current export method, data-processing schedule, sub-processor contract details and restoration process before loading personal or confidential material.

uk-operator.value: Three Rings identifies its operator as Three Rings CIC, company 06820837 registered in England and Wales; Companies House lists the active CIC in Witney.

volunteer-workflow.value: Supplier describes rota self-sign-up or allocation, a volunteer directory, email and SMS communications, statistics, role-limited document sharing and administration tools.

pricing-and-access.value: Supplier states that pricing is annual and turnover-based, gives illustrative prices from about £174 to about £270 including VAT, may offer free access to the smallest organisations, and offers both a demo and free trial.

data-handling.value: Supplier's public terms and GDPR statement describe controller/processor roles, UK and EEA storage arrangements, access controls, action logging, contractual sub-processor restrictions and termination handling.

editorial.assessment: Three Rings is a mature UK general charity-sector option for a church whose immediate problem is volunteer coordination rather than member management. It has a clearer public accountability and data-handling position than many small rota products, alongside a turnover-linked annual price. The service is not church-specific: it does not publicly claim church directory, giving, service planning, safeguarding-case or pastoral-care functionality, so a church should keep its evaluation focused on volunteer administration.
bestFor: Churches with recurring teams that need volunteer self-sign-up, allocation and communications
Churches wanting to replace separate rota spreadsheets, contact lists and shared files
Charitable church projects that value an identified UK CIC and published controller-processor terms

limitations: A general charity-sector tool, not church-specific software
Supplier eligibility is limited to charities and community organisations
Published pricing is illustrative and turnover-based rather than a simple fixed tier table
The service is not presented as a giving, accounting, worship-planning, safeguarding-case or pastoral-care system
Confirm data export, SMS supplier, support response practicalities and confidential-file permissions in a live test

procurementVerdict.problem: Coordinating volunteer shifts, team contact and shared resources without maintaining several separate systems
procurementVerdict.differentiator: A volunteer-run UK CIC with a broad volunteer-administration workflow and unusually detailed public controller-processor terms
procurementVerdict.firstCheck: Run one non-sensitive ministry rota through signup, allocation, absence, messages, role permissions, reporting and export; then review its turnover-based invoice and current data-processing documentation before importing the full volunteer directory
